issues.current: Medicaid revenue is modeled at the $91.10 base per diem only. The checklist concludes the 30% and 70% Medicaid mixes lose money. The tier note says other tier thresholds were not verified.
issues.correct: P.L. 2023, c.80 adds a statutory tier per diem on top of the minimum for ALRs and CPCHs. At 15% to under 30% Medicaid the add-on is $10. At 30% to under 50% it is $15. At 50% to under 70% it is $30. At 70% or more it is $35. The census is the yearly average from paid claims, measured against total licensed beds. The DHS notice says the tier enhancements remain unchanged. The 10% mixes (below 15%) earn no add-on.
issues.evidence: Statute: "those assisted living residences ... at least 30 percent but less than 50 percent ... $15 higher than the minimum per diem"; "at least 70 percent shall receive a per diem rate that is $35 higher". DHS notice: "The tiered rate enhancements based on Medicaid volume will remain unchanged."
issues.fix: Add a tier add-on line to alr40_med30 and alr40_med70, or label the add-on explicitly as unmodeled upside. Because the census is measured against licensed beds, at under 100% occupancy a nominal 70% mix may land in the $30 tier. A nominal 30% mix may land in the $10 tier. Rework the 'lose money' statement in checklist item 1 for those two mixes. Confirm with DMAHS how the add-on stacks on the new $91.10 base.

issues.json_path: staffing.*[role='Director of nursing / RN'] and the checklist item i=40 text 'RN and nursing minimums ... were not verified'
issues.current: RN modeled at 80 hrs/month (20 units), 173 hrs (40 units) and 260 hrs (60 units). Notes say nursing minimums were not verified, and no cost for continuous RN availability is modeled.
issues.correct: N.J.A.C. 8:36-8.2 requires at least one registered professional nurse available at all times. A 2004 ASPE summary says an RN must be on staff or on call 24 hours a day, and that each resident gets an RN assessment and care plan. The 80-hour RN line has no on-call, relief or contract RN cost covering the other hours.
issues.evidence: "A facility shall have at least one registered professional nurse available at all times." (N.J.A.C. 8:36-8.2)
issues.fix: Cite 8:36-8.2 and replace the 'not verified' note. Add a 24/7 RN availability cost (on-call stipend or contract RN) to the 20-unit model. Confirm with DOH what 'available' means for coverage and response time.

issues.current: Statewide NJ home health aide wages are used: $21.43 (75th percentile), $17.83 (median) and $16.67 (25th percentile). The lease benchmark, though, is the Newark HMFA (Essex, Morris, Sussex, Union).
issues.correct: The statewide percentiles match O*NET (BLS 2025 data). The same source's New York-Newark-Jersey City metro figures are $18.60 (25th percentile), $19.08 (median) and $21.05 (75th percentile). A Newark-area site would therefore pay higher median and 25th-percentile wages than modeled. The 'additional employee' at $17.83 and housekeeping at $16.67 sit below the local 25th percentile of $18.60.
issues.fix: Either use metro-level OEWS wages for the Newark site, or drop the Newark rent benchmark and use statewide figures consistently. Re-cost the 24/7 additional-employee line (1,460 hrs/month across both floor roles) and the housekeeping line at the local wages. All modeled wages still clear the $15.92 minimum.

issues.json_path: startup_costs[item='Certificate of Need preparation'] and fees_and_timelines_in_checklist[i=12,14] ('fee ... unverified')
issues.current: CON filing fee is described as unconfirmed. The line is $15,000 to $40,000 for consultant, legal and application costs.
issues.correct: DOH's long-term-care full-review CON instructions (N.J.A.C. 8:33 Appendix B) set a filing fee of $7,500 for total project cost up to $1,000,000. Above $1,000,000 it is $7,500 plus 0.25% of total project cost. The fee must accompany the application. The 40-unit and 60-unit builds exceed $1M, so the fee is roughly $12,000 to $16,000 or more. Whether expedited review for new assisted living uses the same fee was not confirmed.
issues.evidence: "$1,000,000 or Less $7,500; Greater Than $1,000,000 $7,500 + 0.25% of TPC"; "Failure to submit the appropriate fee at the time of filing will result in the application not being accepted".
issues.fix: Add a separate mandatory CON filing fee line. Use $7,500 plus 0.25% of total project cost above $1M as a placeholder. Confirm the expedited-review fee with CN&L at 609-292-6552. State clearly whether the $15k–$40k consultant range includes it.

issues.current: The new-employer UI rate is 'disputed (2.8% vs 2.6825%)'.
issues.correct: There is no dispute. The NJDOL Table C new-employer rate of 2.8% is 2.6825% UI plus 0.1175% Workforce Development/Supplemental Workforce Fund. The employer TDI rate of 0.5% for new employers and the $44,800 wage base are consistent with the sources. The FY2026-27 table (7/1/2026 to 6/30/2027) also shows 2.8%. Modeled payroll tax is 7.65% + 2.8% + 0.5% = 10.95%, rounded to 11%.
issues.fix: Replace 'disputed' with 'new-employer 2.8% combined = 2.6825% UI + 0.1175% WFD/SWF (NJDOL Table C FY2026-27)'. Cite the NJDOL table instead of the Monaco CPA guide.
